summary: Iteration 7 — LID pairing flow fully verified. Created /app/backend/tests/test_lid_pairing.py with 9 scenarios covering the WhatsApp LID pairing lifecycle: pre-pairing rejection with LID hint, /whatsapp/pairing-code generation, wrong-code ignore, right-code pairing via embedded digits, canonical owner-phone persistence for LID-sender messages, code single-use after consumption, DELETE /owner-ids/{id} unpair, settings hides pairing_code/pairing_expires_at, from_pn alt-phone owner recognition, and /whatsapp/check-connection→400 on mock provider. All 9 new tests pass. Regression suites test_webhook_diagnostics.py (16 tests) and test_security_hardening.py (11 tests) pass serially (36/36). Only one flake occurs under pytest-xdist parallel: test_webhook_hmac_signature vs test_security_hardening race on wa9x_webhook_secret (pre-existing, not related to LID feature). Also patched test_webhook_diagnostics.py::test_webhook_log_shape allowlist to include the new 'paired' outcome introduced by this feature. Final state: owner_ids=[], pairing_code=null, provider=mock.

minor.issue: Under pytest-xdist parallel scheduling this test races with test_security_hardening.py which also mutates settings.wa9x_webhook_secret; the concurrent DELETE from another worker wipes the secret between set and POST, causing 401. Serially the test passes. Not caused by the LID feature. Consider @pytest.mark.serial or scope-lock, or a distinct-per-test secret.

action_items: (Optional) Guard the pairing-code exact-match check with constant-time comparison (secrets.compare_digest) on server.py line 247 — currently uses '==' which is fine because the sender is already whitelisted or unknown, but better hygiene.
(Optional) test_webhook_hmac_signature and test_security_hardening both mutate the shared settings.wa9x_webhook_secret — mark them serial or use separate settings docs to eliminate the xdist race.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:247 — the pairing code comparison uses '==' on the digits-only substring of msg.text. This works, but a constant-time compare (secrets.compare_digest) is preferable for a secret token.

server.py:250 — new_ids filter includes both msg.sender and msg.alt_sender but skips values that match owner_number; good. However if alt_sender is a phone number matching owner, only the LID is added (correct behaviour).

wa_provider.py:231 — the swap that prefers phone-alt over LID only fires when the primary looks like a LID; when a message payload has both from=<phone> and from_pn=<phone>, no swap happens (also correct).

server.py:736-737 — status exposes pairing_code only if not expired; nice. pairing_expires_at is exposed only when pairing_code is truthy, which is slightly asymmetric with the check for expiry (a code that has just expired would report pairing_code=null but if s.pairing_code string still truthy would attempt to serialise expires_at — minor cosmetic).

success_rate.backend: 100% (36/36 serial; 35/36 parallel due to pre-existing xdist race)

seed_data_creation: None. Cleanup fixture removes any LID entries before and after the module; final owner_ids=[], pairing_code=null, provider=mock.
